misconceptions.description: Treating a classroom fit matrix as a universal feature checklist rather than a context-specific instrument
misconceptions.trigger: learner reuses generic criteria and weights without tying them to this classroom
misconceptions.feedback: Tie the criteria and weights to your learners, unit, and constraints. A fit matrix is contextual, not a universal checklist.

misconceptions.description: Letting an aggregate fit score override a non-negotiable constraint that should gate the decision
misconceptions.trigger: learner picks the higher total even though it fails a must-have criterion
misconceptions.feedback: Make hard constraints gate the decision. A deal-breaker should remove a tool before scoring, not be averaged into the total.

misconceptions.description: Accepting AI-assigned fit-matrix cells as verified classroom evidence
misconceptions.trigger: learner adopts AI-filled scores without verifying them against the tool and the room
misconceptions.feedback: AI scores are hypotheses. Verify each cell against the actual tool and your classroom before trusting it.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a fit-matrix verdict transfers unchanged to a different classroom
misconceptions.trigger: learner reuses another room's matrix without revisiting weights or criteria
misconceptions.feedback: Fit is relative to context. Re-examine the criteria and weights for the new learners and constraints before reusing the verdict.
